description: Revive brief-0's CholeskyQR2 for n512 good subset: it lost (2408us) mainly because its Gram G=A^T A was a 5.8ms FP32 SIMT GEMM (the single biggest item). Replace that Gram with an int-Ozaki INT8 tensor-core Gram - the SAME technique already used in this kernel's n4096 arm (so it is stock INT8 MMA, remote-portable, NOT a cuBLAS emulation mode). int-Ozaki decomposes FP32 into INT8 slices, does the GEMM on INT8 tensor cores, recomposes to FP32-accuracy. This attacks the dominant cost of the CQR2 path; combined with the existing tensor-core blocked TRSM + fast orhr_col recon, measure whether CQR2 (GEMM-bound, no serial Householder panel) can now beat the FP16 blocked-Householder on the n512 good subset. Stock-only; keep gate margin.

int-Ozaki INT8 tensor-core Gram for the n512 CQR2 G1,G2 (reused the n4096 arm's oz_slice/oz_gram_gemm_grouped/oz_recombine_2pass). INT8 IMMA GEMM cuts the Gram GEMM 5.84ms->2.42ms (confirms brief), but FP64 chol of FP64 G (potrf_*<double> ~10ms vs FP32 ~4.5ms) + int-Ozaki recombine (~3.7ms) + slice (~1ms) overhead -> shape3=38929us, shape7(mixed)=43918us. geomean 2455.6us, slightly regresses parent 2408. Validate clean: n512 factor scaled ~0.0085-0.019 (gate 1.0, ~52x margin), orth ~0.38-0.52 (gate 1.0, ~2x). FP64 chol is the new bottleneck.

FP32 cholesky on the int-Ozaki (exact) G: residuals BYTE-IDENTICAL to FP64 chol (n512 factor scaled ~0.0085-0.019, orth ~0.38-0.52) -- the exact Gram + 2-pass CQR2 + tau-override carry accuracy without FP64 potrf. shape3 38929->36689us, shape7 43918->39598us, geomean 2455.6->2422.6. FP64->FP32 chol saved ~1.5ms but int-Ozaki recombine (FP64, ~3.7ms) + slice (~1ms) overhead still keeps shape3 > parent's 34.57ms. Next: FP32-output recombine (halve its memory traffic) + NS sweep (tau-override owns orth, factor has 52x margin).

NS sweep for the n512 int-Ozaki Gram (added _N512_OZ_NS, separate from the n4096 _OZ_NS=4). KEY FINDING: NS=4/3/2 ALL give byte-identical residuals (factor scaled 0.0085-0.019, orth 0.4-0.52) -- the factor residual is SOLVE-bound not Gram-bound (the tau-override owns orth), so the coarsest 2-slice Gram suffices for this path. NS=2 (npairs=3, half the GEMM+recombine of NS=4): shape3 35968(NS3)/34415(NS2)us, geomean 2414(NS3)/2396.5(NS2). NS=2 now beats parent 2408 and edges the FP32-SIMT-Gram shape3 (34570). Picked NS=2. Profile next to see the new floor (potrf/TRSM/recon dominate).

FP32-output int-Ozaki recombine (new C++ kernels oz_recombine_S_v2_f32 / oz_recombine_GfromS_f32 + wrapper oz_recombine_2pass_f32): S+G stored FP32, weighted sum still FP64-accumulated, only the store narrows. Halves the recombine bandwidth (S/G 1.34GB FP64 -> 0.67GB FP32 at B640 n512). Validates identical residuals. shape3 34415->33139us, geomean 2396.5->2385.8. The int-Ozaki Gram (GEMM 0.9ms + recombine ~1.5ms + slice ~1ms) is now lean. Non-Gram floor (FP32 potrf ~7ms + TRSM ~7ms + orhr_col recon ~6ms) now dominates.

TRSM nb sweep for the n512 CQR2 right-TRSM (tri_solve_right_inv): nb=128 (shape3 33139us, geomean 2386) BEATS nb=256 (35777/2416) and nb=64 (34971/2423). Kept nb=128 (identical code to trial 4). The TRSM ~7ms is algorithm/occupancy-bound at this batch, not nb-bound. Diagnostic: on shape3 (cond=2 dense) the int-Ozaki EXACT Gram cuts the CQR2-rejected count 35/640 (FP32 Gram, brief-0) -> 13/640 (colnorm_dev up to 556 -- the genuine high-cond tail, cond up to 8.8e6); those 13 still route to the mixed-driver fallback (underfilled panel_solve_fused etc).

TRSM diagonal-solve precision exploration (coordinator dir.1: put the solve on tensor cores). ncu: the TRSM batch_trsm_left (diag pre-invert) is 72% occupied / 71% SM-compute / 3.5% DRAM = compute-bound FP32-SIMT, NOT occupancy-starved. Tried tensor-core diagonal solve: prec=2 3xTF32 REGRESSED (shape3 33139->34053us -- nb=128 128x128 blocks too small for 3 GEMMs+hi/lo splits to beat 1 SIMT GEMM), prec=1 single-TF32 was faster (31759) but FAILED the diff_correctness+invariance guards (10-bit diagonal solve loses the factor residual on re-seeded n512 batches). Kept prec=0 (safe+fastest at this block size). geomean 2382 (=trial4 within noise). KEY ncu finding: the recon panel_solve_fused_kernel<64> is the real occupancy bottleneck -- 12.5% THEORETICAL occupancy (64-element float y[W] register array + 32KB smem cap it to ~1 block/SM), 19% SM, 8% DRAM, latency-starved. That n4096-tuned kernel wastes 87% of the machine at n512 B640.
